⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **218** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **157** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **157**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **102** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fafe515edaf84aeba42f3bc90a1c6aff95a138a7` — the merge of head `7d079947412d31180bc9427968bca044dc0b9554` into base `c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fafe515edaf84aeba42f3bc90a1c6aff95a138a7 && git checkout fafe515edaf84aeba42f3bc90a1c6aff95a138a7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953 7d079947412d31180bc9427968bca044dc0b9554 && git checkout -B drift-repro c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953 && git merge --no-ff 7d079947412d31180bc9427968bca044dc0b9554

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c76c0e042ea1efc9ccb7b209a82dd8f0fc119953` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

What the delta changes, each judged:

1. **The closed nested twins now share the open shapes' field instances** (`retryConfigShape` and `connectorActionShape` are built once through `sharedFields`; the open `RetryConfigSchema` / `ConnectorActionSchema` and the module-private `AuthoredRetryConfigSchema` / `AuthoredConnectorActionSchema` hold the same instances, pinned by identity in the spec test). **Right, and necessary.** On `main` the open `integration/RetryConfig` and `integration/ConnectorAction` defs were reachable from the `connector` root through the open nested shapes of the entry (root-graph); on the first head the closed entry carried its own twin instances, so the authorable-surface gate (`computeSurfaceReachability`) reached neither open def from any root and a bare deletion of one of their baseline lines would have been waived as over-collection — the regression that reddened CI. Sharing the instances makes the gate reach each open def through its derived-clone bridge (same name, same instance in a visited object node), so a bare deletion is refused again unless it carries its proof. The published surface is unchanged: the twins emit no def, and the net diff carries no change under `packages/spec/api-surface`, `authorable-surface`, `authorable-defaults`, `export-origins`, `declaration-map`, `json-schema`, or `content/docs/references` (verified against the net file list; the only artifact in the diff is the strictness-ledger count shard, 4 → 6).
2. **The `computeGuidanceRoutes` reasoning `connectorBaseShape`'s docblock records** — read against the gate. The census pairs an emitted def with a `strictObject` declaration by shape signature and by the identity of every field, so with shared instances the open `integration/RetryConfig` and `integration/ConnectorAction` defs now pair with their twins' declarations and are read as owing the twins' prescriptions. That pairing is consulted in one place only: check (c) proof 4, for a baseline line the build stopped emitting on that def. A deleted baseline line of an open def can only name a key that def once declared, and every key the twins' guidance names — the credential-shaped keys, and `method` / `path` / `url` on an action — is one the open defs never declared (the census itself drops a guidance entry filed under a declared key). So no deletion of these defs can reach the pairing today, and the open defs are not charged anything. The one way it could in future — a guidance entry added to a twin for a key the open def declares, and that key later deleted — yields a `declared-but-silent` violation, which refuses the deletion rather than waiving it: a louder outcome, never a softer one, and the alias-integrity audit flags such an entry as a false claim before that. The top-level reasoning stays as written (`connectorBaseShape` is still a function, and the closed entry keeps its own top-level instances); the nested docblock records why the cost does not bite one level down. **Right.**
3. **S2 delivered**: both twins carry the entry's credential-key guidance (one shared, frozen table, also spread into the top-level entry's guidance), the action twin additionally answers `method`, `path`, `url` with the ADR-0097 §5 prescription, and the action's own `key` is excluded from the credential table because it is a declared key. Pinned per key, with the value never echoed. The nested changeset's "Now" bullet is updated to say so. **Right.**
4. **S3 delivered in part**: the dogfood pins an inline `providerConfig.spec` document — a URL inside it holding a credential query parameter is refused at `providerConfig.spec.servers.0.url` (the write door's array-element position), and a document whose URLs are credential-free saves as written (saved disabled, so the pin is the door's answer). **Right.** The `retryConfig: {}` pin is not added, consistent with ③(b) being escalated rather than ruled.
5. **Moved CI fixtures** (question 2):

   - `packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.deleted-baseline.test.ts` — the `#17356` specimen moves from `integration/RetryConfig` (two hops under the unregistered `connector` root; after this PR reachable only through the derived-clone bridge) to `integration/DeclarativeConnectorEntry`, the root's own def. The test's named claim ("a def rooted only in an UNREGISTERED kind is reachable, and a genuinely unreachable one still is not") is measured with unchanged regexes in both regimes, and the entry def's only root is indeed the unregistered kind. What the old specimen carried incidentally — that the walk descends two hops beneath an unregistered root and reports a root-graph hit there — is no longer measured by this pin. **Measures its claim; narrower on depth** (should-fix S4 below, low weight).
6. **Everything carried forward from the first record holds on this head** (question 4): the URL refusal and its one walk shared with the read, the read's rewrite of the `auth` endpoints, the open exports' posture, the save door's order (parse, gate, carry-forward, put) and the no-migration posture, `_diagnostics` on the raw stored body, no new public export, the ledger shard delta, and the forced test edits — each re-read on this head's tree where the delta touched it and unchanged where it did not.

- **(a) The whole userinfo, including a bare token before the host — within the ruling.** Unchanged: the ruling binds the write to the redactor's own traversal and judgement, the redactor on `main` already withheld the whole userinfo, and the built-in providers reach their upstream through `fetch`, which refuses a URL carrying any userinfo, so no dispatchable configuration is lost. No finding.
- **(b) `retryConfig: {}` over a stored row holding a withheld nested key — escalate (unchanged).** Omitting `retryConfig` removes it with its withheld keys (pinned); `retryConfig: {}` keeps the withheld key at rest under the protocol's per-path carry-forward, which grafts into any container the incoming body still carries. The acceptance says 「明确清除(`{}`)才删除」; the tree reads omission as the explicit clear. The substance holds (a served-form save loses nothing; the author has a clear), the letter does not, the diff touches no protocol code, the carry-forward's reading of an empty container is type-wide, and the PR discloses it. A maintainer decides: either omission is the explicit clear and this PR stands, or an empty container becomes a clear in the protocol's carry-forward — a `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` change with its own declaration and pins. Whichever wins should be pinned (S3's remaining half).
- **(c) Header and environment maps outside the write walk — consistent with 「用和脱敏器相同的遍历」.** Unchanged: the redactor's traversal never enters those maps (withheld whole before the URL walk; the shared walk returns at a map path), so the same traversal excludes them by construction, pinned "judged by neither". The lane-seat note stands: the PR body's claim that the authoring lint warns on a credential-shaped literal inside a map is not in `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-authoring-lint.ts` on `main`; the ruling does not ask for one.
- **(d) An inline OpenAPI document under `providerConfig.spec` walked at the write door — acceptable narrowing within the ruling, now pinned at the HTTP door.** 「`providerConfig` 各层 URL」 is every level; the read on `main` already walked an inline document; the provider accepts an inline object, an http(s) URL or a package file path and never parses a JSON string inline, so no inline form escapes the walk. The cost (a document whose example URL carries a credential-named parameter with a value is packaged as a file) is declared.
- **(e) `defineConnector()` does not run the URL refusal — conforming.** Unchanged: the ruling places the rule in the entry's refinement; `DefineConnectorSchema` has parsed the closed base without the ADR-0097 / ADR-0143 refinements since the top-level close, stores nothing, and every stack door re-parses its value; the nested close does apply there and each changeset lists the doors it binds.

### ④ Design judgment

- **`packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts`** — holds on this head. `sharedFields` memoises each shape's field set once per process; zod 4 field schemas are immutable, `strictObject` builds its closed object around the shared shape without touching the fields, and the declaration it registers carries that same shape, which is exactly what makes the gate's identity bridge reach the open defs. The twins stay module-private; the open exports keep their posture (pinned); the refusal messages name the surface, the keys and the prescription, never a value (pinned). `connectorBaseShape` stays a per-carrier function at the top level, and the nested docblocks state why sharing is safe one level down (see ① item 2). **Should-fix S1 (open item, carried forward)**: one item on the shared URL module is carried to the maintainer outside this record; it is a should-fix, not a must-fix, and does not block the verdict. (Its detail is withheld from this public copy by the seat.)
- **`packages/spec/src/integration/connector-url-credentials.ts`** — unchanged between heads; the first record's judgment stands (holds against `credentialQueryParamOf` / `urlCredentialQueryParams` / the redactor's userinfo regex; every input form tried is judged identically by both doors; `connectorUrlCredentialPositionOf` is right).
- **`packages/spec/src/integration/connector-credential-redaction.ts`** — unchanged between heads; the first record's judgment stands (a carry-forward of `main`'s behaviour on the shared walk; removals first; `auth` endpoints rewritten in place; served `auth` stays declared keys only).
- **The two D3 entries** — unchanged between heads; consistent with the tree.
- **Tests** — the spec pins now also cover each prescription the twins carry and the field-instance identity the gate relies on; the dogfood adds the inline-document refusal and its control. **Should-fix S3 (remaining half)**: pin `retryConfig: {}` once ③(b) is ruled. **Should-fix S4 (low)**: the `#17356` pin now holds the unregistered root's own def; keep a specimen beneath that root too (an instance-auth kind reached through `connector.auth` stays root-graph in the closed entry), so the walk's descent beneath an unregistered root is measured again and not only its enumeration.
- **Cited-code cross-checks** — `reachabilityRootTypes()` unions the registered types with the unregistered kinds, so `connector` is a root and the closed entry is visited; `computeSurfaceReachability().reachableVia` answers `derived-clone` for a def whose shape entry (same name, same instance) appears in a visited node, which is what the shared instances give the two open defs; `verdictFor` is reached only from the deleted-baseline branch of check (c). The strictness ledger's hand-written `integration/` row (`docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.md`) still describes only the top-level close with its own-instances reasoning; a sentence on the two twins and their shared instances would keep it current — a docs matter for the lane seat, not a tree finding.

Delivered since the first record — S2 (guidance on both twins), S3's inline-document pin. Escalate — ③(b), the `{}` reading of the acceptance (unchanged).

### ④ Design judgment

- **`connector-url-credentials.ts`** — holds against `credentialQueryParamOf` / `urlCredentialQueryParams` / `decodeQueryKey` (the query runs from the first `?` to the fragment, pairs split on `&`, key percent- and plus-decoded, matched case-insensitively, an empty value carries nothing) and against `URL_USERINFO_RE` (every class excludes `/?#`, so the `@` must sit in the authority and the greedy class backtracks to the last `@` before the path). Tried to break the walk: a percent-encoded name (`api%5Fkey`) is judged; a credential name in the fragment or with an empty value is not, at both doors; a `?` inside the fragment is fragment text at both doors; `user@`, `user:pass@` and `a@b@` are each one userinfo at both doors; a URL in a nested array (`providerConfig.x.0.0`) is refused at its index and withheld at `providerConfig.x` whole; a dotted key holding an object holding a URL is refused at the leaf and withheld at the dotted key whole; a string the module's own stated rule does not read as a URL is judged by neither door (the boundary ③a is about, held by the maintainer); `providerConfig` or `auth` that is not a plain object is walked by neither (and refused by the entry's own shapes). `connectorUrlCredentialPositionOf` is right: the first non-addressable hop ends the position, and the protocol's `resolveRedactedPath` tries the standard split first and longer trailing keys last, so a withheld dotted key is re-grafted by its whole-string name.
- **Read/write symmetry — holds.** The rewriter and the detector share the pair predicate and the same `?` / `#` / `&` boundaries, and the userinfo is removed by the same regex, so the served URL re-judged at the write door holds no credential part: a save of the served form is accepted and the carry-forward re-grafts the stored URL where the incoming equals the served one (pinned at the HTTP door for the oauth2 endpoints; an edit stores the edit). A stored array or dotted key the read withholds whole is absent from the served form, so a served-form save re-grafts it and the position check keeps it (the redactor withholds it again where it lands). The dedicated spec pin walks eight URL forms through both doors in both roots and asserts refused ⇔ rewritten.
